findings.failure_path: A tool authorization is revoked while a model invocation is running. Because mutation is forbidden during that invocation, it completes against the old tool set and can return a call to the revoked tool. The new rule resets the cache and restarts only afterward, but never requires the runtime to invalidate or reject completions and tool calls from the prior authorization/tool generation; therefore stale output can still reach the executor and external channel.
findings.smallest_fix: On any authorization, privacy, safety, or policy invalidation, immediately advance an authorization/tool generation; bind every invocation and tool call to that generation, reject stale completions before tool execution, and reauthorize the call against the current generation before permitting side effects.

concern_results.conclusion: Checked the invalidation/eviction path, normalized cache counters and batch fallback, tool-set and trifecta controls, delegation gates, register claims, and vendor-number framing. The material bypass is that revocation during an in-flight invocation has no generation fence preventing the stale completion from requesting an external action.

challenge_focus: Adversarial pass on the lane-4 candidate: (1) the eviction-vs-invalidation clause — a revoked or invalidated tool that still survives in definitions, history, or cache generation, or a restart/fail-closed path that loses accepted work; (2) normalized cache-usage counters and the batch capability decision — a provider shape that still double-counts, misclassifies, duplicates billing, or orphans work; (3) the tool-set boundary, plan-then-execute binding, and trifecta negative test — any injected or stale path that still reaches an external action; (4) the delegation fan-out gate, effort_budget, artifact-not-relay, MAST classification, hub-vs-peer default — bypass-by-omission or over-broad cost; (5) register anchors, receipts, rows — stale locators, unsupported claims, contradictions; (6) vendor numbers as invariants, wrong ids, leakage.
